summary.name: ml0x
summary.one_liner: ml0x is a four-stage pipeline (analyze, implement, test, review) that wraps Claude Code with non-bypassable budget caps and quality gates, with a free MIT-licensed core and a paid full system.
keywords: rout llm requests to cheaper model
use_cases: Keeping Claude Code spending under a fixed budget
Running coding agents through analyze, test and review gates before seeing output
Routing simple queries to a cheaper model to cut token costs
Automating multi-step feature work with an AI coding agent
summary.what_it_does: The page describes ml0x as a 4-stage pipeline around Claude Code: analyze, implement, test and review. It adds budget limits that the author says cannot be bypassed, and quality gates that run before any output is shown. The page claims model routing sends most queries to a cheaper model (Flash at $0.28/M output versus Opus at $75/M) and cites 90% prompt cache hits, but these are the author's stated figures. The core is described as free and open source on GitHub under MIT, with the full system sold once for $99 and a 60-day refund window. The page also lists related pipeline products and free Chrome extensions and calculators by the same author.
notable: Budget caps described as impossible to bypass, enforced before quality gates
Four stages: analyze, implement, test, review, with gates before output is shown
MIT-licensed core on GitHub; full system is a one-time $99 purchase with 60-day refund
Model routing claims: most queries sent to a cheaper model, with prompt caching
caveats: Full system costs $99 once; only the core is free and open source
Savings figures (-85%, 90% cache hit, 74% routed to Flash) are the author's own claims, not independently verified
Page is largely promotional and mixes the product with unrelated free tools by the same author
